Possibly even enough to pull him loose entirely. “Alright.” He nodded. “When I say go, I need you to put everything on it. Don’t pull — press. Get as much weight behind it as you can.” Dwight looked dubious. “You realize I have the upper body strength of wet spaghetti, right?” “You don’t need it. Just put your weight into it. It doesn’t need to move much. I’d do it but I’ve seen you favoring that arm. You’re not going to be able to pull him free.” Dwight winced a bit, flexing against the throb in his arm, but nodded and moved to brace himself against the bar. Felix took his place at the gap he had carved out, easily slipping between the stones before calling out for him to start shoving. He leaned his whole weight into the bar — back bowed, knees shaking, blood dripping from his elbow — and couldn’t help but grin a bit as he felt something on the other side give way. Just a few inches. But it was something. Felix dove further into the pocket of space, immediately scraping aside whatever rubble remained over David’s chest and arm. Not all of it. There wasn’t room. But he could move . He could touch . He could see the stuttering rise and fall of David’s ribs. Hear the dry rasp of breath in his throat. It didn’t sound healthy, or even stable for that matter, but it was more than it had been. It would have to be enough. Between the two of them, they managed it. The slab lifted just enough — Dwight grunting, legs shaking, throwing everything he had into the bar — and Felix got an arm under David’s shoulders and pulled . The pressure gave with a low, grinding groan. As soon as the weight shifted, the rest of the stones seemed to settle on their own, collapsing inward to fill the space he left behind. A few sharp edges scraped his legs on the way out. Ripped cloth. Skin. Nothing critical. Nothing a simple medkit couldn’t fix. He had gotten lucky in that aspect, the rubble along his legs having been no worse off for him than a hook injury. Probably less so. Even then, it didn’t matter. They had him. Felix dragged David clear, huffing from the exertion as he laid him out on the flat stone behind them. Dwight dropped the bar and scrambled over, falling to his knees beside them. “David—? Come on, man — talk to me—” He reached out and shook his shoulder — gently, but desperate — and the stillness was deafening. “Is he —? “ “Pulse is still there. He’s just not breathing right.” Felix set to easing David’s shoulders up to rest along his lap. He tipped his head back carefully, opening his airway the way he’d seen medics do, the extra space granting a light wheeze from him as his eyelids fluttered lightly. “There you go,” Felix muttered, brushing dust from his face. “You’re not allowed to check out on me now.” Dwight let out a strained huff as he hovered nearby, clearly not sure how to be of help. He looked down at David’s arm, bits of skin visible through the torn sleeve of his jacket. The damage was clear. Bruises were already forming in lurid shades of red and violet, crawling up from the wrist to the shoulder in uneven splotches. It didn’t look broken, but that arm was going to scream when it finally woke back up. Maybe it was better that he was still out. “I don’t understand why this keeps happening. It was never like this...” “I thought you guys were always fighting to not die in these trials?” “Not like this!” Dwight stared at David, trying to will him to wake up. “There was structure. Ritual. Patterns. You’re too new to the Fog; you wouldn’t know. But this kind of shit? This never happened. I don’t know what to DO anymore.” “Think maybe punching him will help too?” Dwight flinched, a light flush blooming across his face. “I said I was sorry —” Felix flashed him a quick smirk, betraying the attempt at defusing the tension, and Dwight visibly uncoiled a bit. “This is all so screwed up now. I didn’t know what else to do...” “No, you made the right call.” Felix ran a hand over David’s chest, frowning at the uneven, shallow movements, the edges of a thought pressing in on his mind. “Although... it might not be the worst idea...” “You want me to hit him? Are you out of your mind?” “No, I mean... hang on.” Felix shifted his grip and pressed two fingers into the muscle just above David’s injured shoulder, digging straight into the bruising that mottled whatever skin was visible. David jerked like he’d been shocked — a raw, hoarse inhale tearing out of him with the pain. His chest hitched violently against it, the air locked behind tightly clenched muscles for a moment, before finally breaking free with an ugly ragged sound. A second wet gasp tore out of him like his body didn’t want to breathe but couldn’t stop trying. Another followed, then a third — until the motion collapsed into a raw, hacking cough that curled him hard onto his side and out of Felix’s grip. His lungs were fighting the return. Like they’d forgotten what breathing felt like and were relearning by force. Each inhale was a frantic jerk, each exhale a failed sob. He choked on air like it was water, body spasming from the effort. Felix muttered something in a language Dwight couldn’t quite catch as he knelt beside David, one hand braced lightly against his back, rubbing slow circles in an attempt to ease the shaking.
